reviews.basis: Schema verification batches metadata reads per table; per-column UPDATE/ALTER operations are migration-only and cannot be represented as one homogeneous bulk DDL statement.
ALTER TABLE is a write/DDL operation, while this Rule Claim is database reads in loops.
One bulk query is issued per distinct party DocType, not per entry; names are deduplicated before querying.
This is deliberate Frappe controller registration. The immutable upstream rule warns about compatibility and app conflicts; it does not establish a defect here.
A remotely callable authenticated method uses permission-bypassing get_all and returns Account identifiers without an explicit role, DocType, or record-level permission check.
Distinct names are intentionally queried in fixed-size chunks; query count scales by batches rather than rows.
The SQL is a deliberately chunked DELETE write, not a read. Chunking protects max_allowed_packet and is operationally appropriate.
The SQL is an UPDATE write. It may warrant separate write/query-count review, but cannot satisfy a read-in-loop claim.
UI-controlled invocation is not authorisation; any authenticated caller can invoke the whitelisted method and get_all bypasses Account permissions.

Selected fields are a fixed local allowlist, remarks length is converted to int, ordering is selected from fixed clauses, and condition values remain parameterised; build_match_conditions is framework-generated SQL.
Names are deduplicated and queried in fixed-size buckets per supported party type, rather than one query per GL entry.

follow_up_reviews.basis: After write exclusions exposed the enclosing read, source review confirmed one information_schema query per configured table; this is startup/schema verification rather than one query per business row.
